edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Rename the empty duplicate dcroat to dcroat.1
edit_verdicts.reason: The source has StartChar: dcroat twice: line 25881 (Encoding 273 273 211, the real glyph) and line 49307 (Encoding 65704 -1 547, Width 0, smcp/aalt only). No Refer or Kerns2 points at 547, so a one-line rename is minimal. The release keeps both glyphs and fontTools reads the second as dcroat.1. GSUB smcp/aalt in release and build are identical. Wording fix: say 'SFD glyph index 547 (release gid 548)'. Tooling fix: the op must go into gf-source-modernization/tools/sfd_edit.py, which land.py applies, not only source_corrections.py. Also, the existing renameglyph on this file exits 0 and leaves TWO 'StartChar: dcroat.1', so it needs a FATAL guard for duplicated names.

edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Take the vertical metrics of Corben-Bold-TTF.sfd
edit_verdicts.reason: The source states typo/win/hhea 2300/-940 with all Offsets 0 (absolute). The first google/fonts binary 90abd17b4 carries exactly 2300/-940, so no FontForge vintage explains 2826. The value is stated by the designer's v1.100 Bold: the -TTF.sfd, and also Corben-Bold.vfb (vfb3ufo: 2826/-969 typo, win and hhea), which they did not read. Honest and minimal. Optionally cite the .vfb in the body.

The source states '    '. FontForge copies a stated vendor (2012 tottf.c:3495-3500), and the 2011 export has '    ', so no fidelity path exists. No Bold source names a vendor (.sfd blank, -TTF.sfd 'PfEd', .vfb empty, OTF NUL). 'newt' comes from the Regular sources and entered the Bold release in 5b1755d5a. The body says this plainly.

The source states Panose: 2 0 5 5 2 0 0 2 0 4, as do the -TTF.sfd and the .vfb. 90abd17b4 and bacec3651 carry 0; 15 first appears in 5b1755d5a. Babelfont's PANOSE fill applies only when none is stated. The edit is explicit and changes only digit 1. Wording fix: the body says both 'exists only in the release' and '15 is what the Regular's sources state'. Suggested: 'No Bold source states it (.sfd, -TTF.sfd, .vfb all give 0); google/fonts 5b1755d5a set 15, the Regular's serif style.'

The outcome is right: with the flag the build adds U+02C9->macron and U+2219->periodcentered, which the release lacks; without it the cmap equals the release and there are still 3 rows. But the cause is the harness rule in baseline.sh (dup=yes whenever the release maps U+00A0 and U+00AD), which misfires wherever those are distinct source glyphs. Corben-Regular misfires too: converting only (no build), the flag adds U+02C9, U+2219 and U+03BC, none of which its release has. Fix the rule (pass the flag only when U+00A0 or U+00AD maps to the same glyph as U+0020 or U+002D, or the release carries a makeotf-only codepoint) instead of a per-style DROP_FLAGS.

verification.overall: Their result holds: I rebuilt every edit independently and reproduced it byte for byte. The build failure comes from a duplicated glyph name (dcroat, SFD glyph index 547), which fontc's job bookkeeping cannot handle. Renaming only index 547 to dcroat.1 builds, and E2 (vertical metrics), E3 (vendor) and E4 (PANOSE) then close 8 rows without opening any. That leaves 3 rows, all converter work already in progress (weight class, x-height, cap height). No FontForge exporter vintage explains any edited value: the original 2011 export carries exactly what the .sfd states, and the 2015 google/fonts commit 5b1755d5a changed only the header tables. The glyph provenance is confirmed and stronger than they claimed. All 551 raw outlines, the advances, the cmap and all kerned pairs match the release, head.created is 8 s after the .sfd was last saved, and the .vfb is a 264-glyph v1.100 master, so it cannot be the source. All 4 edits are kept; E1 and E4 need small wording fixes. The flag drop should be done as a baseline.sh rule fix, since Corben-Regular misfires too. Beyond this unit: the table gate ignores the diffenator3 kerning report and accepts GPOS differences without shaping, a gap for every family; the existing renameglyph silently re-creates the duplicate here; and the new op has to be added to sfd_edit.py. The report is at /home/fsanches/compartilhado/gf-source-modernization/investigations/corben-bold/VERIFY.md.
